FinKore makes recurring financial behavior explicit so you can understand a rule, implement it in your own stack, and evaluate the result against a shared contract. Start with the financial question your product needs to answer.

You can begin with one domain. You do not need to adopt every part of FinKore at once.

Understand what you are adopting

FinKore publishes a specification, portable acceptance cases, and an Agentic Contract for machine clients. Your team owns the implementation and its integration into your product.

The repository provides the contract and tools that validate its published artifacts. Financial implementations and execution of acceptance cases belong to consumers. There is no financial package to install or hosted service to connect to here.

For more context, read About the project.

Follow the contract from principle to evidence

Read the CoreDoc first. Its principles explain why monetary integrity, controlled state, preserved history, approvals, and identity need explicit obligations.

The domain specifications turn those obligations into precise requirements, invariants, and portable errors. They are authoritative for financial behavior.

The conformance artifacts connect requirements to portable inputs and expected observations. They help you evaluate your own implementation; publishing a case does not mean it has been executed or prove that an implementation conforms.

The Agentic Contract describes canonical operation semantics for machine clients. Your integration provides execution and authorization infrastructure while preserving the specification's behavior.

Walk through one rounding case

The README example starts with 10.005 EUR rounded to scale 2. Follow that same amount from its financial obligation to a published expected observation. This walkthrough illustrates the existing contract; it adds no rounding policy to your product.

1. Read the obligation and requirements

CORE-001.2 requires exact calculation and a declared rule when reducing precision. A currency's customary minor-unit scale is not itself a rounding instruction.

In Money Rounding, MONEY-ROUNDING-001 requires an explicit target scale and mode. MONEY-ROUNDING-003 defines the supported modes. At a tie, HALF_UP selects the nearest candidate farther from zero; HALF_EVEN selects the nearest candidate whose last retained digit is even. For 10.005 EUR at scale 2, those rules give different results.

2. Discover the existing cases

Open conformance/manifest.json, find the suite whose id is money, and follow its vectorFiles entry ./money/rounding.json, resolved relative to the manifest directory. In that declared file, locate these stable IDs:

Vector IDModeExpected amountCurrency
money.round.half-up.tie-positive-001HALF_UP10.01EUR
money.round.half-even.tie-even-down-001HALF_EVEN10.00EUR

Both cases supply 10.005 EUR and scale: 2. Discover files only through the manifest; do not enumerate the Money directory. The traceability index connects requirements to their published cases and coverage limits.

3. Read the request and complete expected observation

This excerpt copies the relevant fields of money.round.half-up.tie-positive-001 from the manifest-listed file:

{
  "id": "money.round.half-up.tie-positive-001",
  "requirements": [
    "MONEY-ROUNDING-002",
    "MONEY-ROUNDING-003",
    "MONEY-ROUNDING-008"
  ],
  "operation": "finkore.money.round",
  "input": {
    "value": {
      "amount": "10.005",
      "currency": "EUR"
    },
    "scale": 2,
    "mode": "HALF_UP"
  },
  "expected": {
    "status": "success",
    "value": {
      "amount": "10.01",
      "currency": "EUR"
    },
    "observations": {
      "operand": {
        "amount": "10.005",
        "currency": "EUR"
      }
    }
  }
}
FieldWhat to look for
idThe stable case identity used to report an evaluation.
requirementsThis case exercises determinism (MONEY-ROUNDING-002), portable mode semantics (MONEY-ROUNDING-003), and currency preservation (MONEY-ROUNDING-008). The explicit request is also governed by MONEY-ROUNDING-001; that ID is not listed by this particular case.
operationThe canonical behavior to map to your own API: finkore.money.round.
inputThe exact decimal amount, currency, explicit target scale, and mode to supply.
expected.valueThe resulting amount and currency, with exactly two fractional digits for this explicit scale.
expected.observations.operandThe unchanged source Money to observe after the operation.

The complete vector also includes spec, a description, tags, and defect intent. The operation contract and Agentic descriptor explain the portable boundary; the fixture shape does not prescribe your production API.

4. Compare your implementation's observations

In your own environment, map the operation to your implementation and supply the case's input. Preserve exact decimal semantics when parsing "10.005"; do not convert it to approximate binary floating point or infer a policy from EUR.

Normalize the actual result according to the consumer guide, then compare the whole observation with expected: success status, 10.01 EUR at scale 2, and the unchanged 10.005 EUR operand. Derive the observation from the actual result and retained source, independently of expected.

Repeat with money.round.half-even.tie-even-down-001, which supplies HALF_EVEN and expects 10.00 EUR with the same unchanged operand. These two cases expose substitution of one tie-breaking mode for the other. Compare exact decimals and the required presentation scale; an approximate tolerance is not a Money comparison rule.

FinKore publishes these expectations. Your team supplies the implementation, invocation, observation, comparison, and reporting tools. Reading the example or running repository artifact checks does not execute either case. Two cases also do not establish conformance to all Money requirements: continue with the implementation workflow to define your scope, select the related success and failure cases, and collect your own execution evidence.

Pick one domain that matches your problem

DomainA useful starting question
MoneyHow should monetary values retain their currency and exact amount through calculation?
WorkflowWhich lifecycle changes are permitted, and what must remain unchanged after rejection?
AuditWhat evidence must be preserved to explain an action and its history?
ApprovalsWhat was approved, for which subject, and does the decision still apply?
Financial EntitiesHow does a financial subject retain its identity through validation and permitted change?

Use the specification index to find the selected domain. For example, if you need monetary values, begin with Money's representation and arithmetic requirements before adding rounding or allocation to your scope. Your product decides its language, API, storage, and business policies.

Build your first slice

  1. Read the selected domain's requirements alongside CoreDoc. Use the conventions and glossary to understand normative language and terminology.
  2. Identify the requirements, portable errors, and observable results you will support. Keep that scope explicit.
  3. Find related acceptance cases through the conformance manifest and requirement traceability.
  4. Implement the behavior in your own codebase. Follow the implementation guide for exact values, deterministic context, and preservation of state when an operation fails.
  5. Use your own tooling to invoke the implementation, observe the result, and compare it with the expected observations. The consumer guide explains the responsibilities and limits of that evaluation.
  6. Add tests for your integration and plausible defects. Document your supported scope and evidence before expanding to another slice.

A useful first milestone is a small, documented scope with traceable requirements, reproducible observations, and coverage of success and failure cases. Acceptance cases provide bounded evidence; add your own checks for the product boundaries you introduce.

When a rule is unclear

Do not infer financial behavior from a fixture, a language default, or a past implementation. Describe the observable result that is undefined, the artifacts you reviewed, plausible interpretations, and their financial or control impact. Follow Contributing to raise the gap for specification-first review.
